# Packaged Chronicle binary observations

[The generated profile](profile.json) captures Chronicle **19.29.4**,
Fundamentals **7.19.6** and .NET/System.Text.Json **10.0.12**. The
[provenance](provenance.json) pins packages, runtime, sources and SHA-256 hashes.
Goldens are generated by the [capture harness](capture/Program.cs), never inferred
from Go's JSON encoder. Ordinary Go tests need neither .NET nor network access.

## Capture boundary

[Isolation](capture/Isolation.cs) is copied unchanged from the enum harness.
It invokes the packaged private client options initializer on an uninitialized
client, then the real EventSerializer constructor. Empty artifacts and an explicit
empty derived catalog prevent discovery; any registry call invalidates capture.
No client constructor, connection, Mongo/BSON converter or kernel runs here.

Both naming policies independently record 11 writes, 51 reads, 22 packaged
Expando conversion pairs and eight schemas (both generator APIs). Typed binary
snapshots retain CLR identity and hexadecimal bytes. JSON text retains escaping,
property order and omission. Errors contain exception categories only; secondary
reserialization and Expando-to-JSON results are independent observations.

## Findings

- Bytes write as padded standard base64 strings; `+` is escaped as `\u002B`.
  Nil properties are omitted; empty bytes write as `""`.
- Binary schemas have string type and `byte-array` format. Nullable binary has
  `["string", "null"]` type and `byte-array?` format. Class properties have no
  required list; the record control requires only `Payload`.
- Missing/null nonnullable binary becomes empty bytes; nullable binary remains
  null. Nested properties and arrays of binary retain their representation.
- Unpadded, short-padding, URL-safe, nonzero-padding-bit and invalid base64 fail.
  Leading space and trailing newline are accepted and reserialize canonically.
- C# accepts null array elements. Go deliberately refuses these and whitespace
  inside base64 strings: this slice admits only canonical, non-null elements.
- Packaged Expando conversion materializes binary as `System.Byte[]` and writes
  canonical base64, including array items. Map schemas are capture controls,
  not evidence of safe kernel dictionary traversal.

## Reproduce

SDK 10.0.401 and runtime 10.0.12 must already be installed. From `capture/`:

```sh
dotnet restore BinaryCapture.csproj --locked-mode
dotnet run --project BinaryCapture.csproj --no-restore -- ../recaptured.json
```

The output path must not exist. Compare the new output with the committed
profile; never overwrite goldens by hand. Build outputs are locally ignored.
Live-kernel admission is separately exercised by the Go integration witness.
Binary arrays remain capture controls, not admitted Go declarations: the pinned
kernel preserves their events but projects them into arrays of empty documents.
Go tests compare an explicitly leaf-only view of these unchanged package goldens
and separately require binary-array registration to fail. See the
[binary parity boundary](../../../Documentation/parity.md#baselines-and-evidence).
